10.0.s.en: (1) The threat of the plague of locusts (the eighth plague)

10.0.0.en: The Lord asked Moses to go in to Pharaoh and ask him to let His people go, but he would refuse, so that God might be glorified in the hardness of his heart, and it would be a lesson for all generations and a strengthening of the faith of God's people throughout the days, so that fathers would teach their children how great is God's power, His protection of His children and His punishment of their enemies.

10.0.1.en: Take care to teach your children faith in God and the Church, so that they may have the spiritual sense and feel God's work in the events around them and live reassured in His care.

10.1.0.en: Moses and Aaron rebuked Pharaoh for not letting God's people go, that he might turn back from the hardness of his heart.

10.2.0.en: Moses also threatened him that if he did not let the people of the children of Israel go, God would strike him with the eighth plague, which is the plague of locusts, which would come in enormous numbers, not only as locusts usually do but in many times the usual swarms, for Egypt had never seen an attack of locusts like it, and it would eat every green thing in Egypt, whether small plants or trees, and would cover not only the fields but also the houses. The "residue of that which is escaped, which remaineth" means the wheat, the rie, the fruit of the trees in which something may have survived, and the grain kept in the open storehouses. Then Moses and Aaron went out of the palace and left him to the hardness of his heart and his distress at the divine threat. This shows the weakness of the Egyptian gods, unable to protect the Egyptians from the locusts that eat their necessary food, for Egypt is an agricultural country, and if its plants were spoiled, it would fall into great hunger.

10.3.0.en: The men of the royal court and Pharaoh's counselors felt the power of the God of the Hebrews, who had ruined Egypt and shown the helplessness of its gods, and they were finally forced to reproach Pharaoh and demand that he let the children of Israel go. Although their opposing Pharaoh could cost them their lives, their severe distress and frustration drove them to it.

10.4.0.en: Pharaoh was moved by his servants' words and was convinced of their truth, for he felt the power of God, so he agreed to the idea of the people going out to worship God. But the hardness of his heart made him refuse to let all the children of Israel go, and he wanted to specify certain classes of them to go out, and in this it appears that his obedience to God was incomplete. We notice that Pharaoh had agreed that they should sacrifice to God in the land of Egypt (ch. 8:25) and Moses refused that; then he agreed again to the children of Israel going out to sacrifice to God, but at a short distance from Egypt (ch. 8:28), and Moses refused that too, insisting on carrying out God's word in full. Here he agreed to their going a three days' journey, but on condition that not all the children of Israel go out.

10.5.0.en: Moses insisted that they all go, young and old, men and women, that is, all the people with their cattle, to worship God and keep a feast to Him.

10.6.0.en: Because of the severity of the plagues that had fallen on Pharaoh and the Egyptians, he tried to trick Moses, pretending to pity the children of Israel, and said that only the men should go and should not take women or children with them, lest they be exposed to the hardships of travel in the desert, such as hunger, thirst and wild animals, "evil is before you." Moses rejected his proposal, and here Pharaoh became angry and drove them out from his presence, for he signaled to his servants and they put them out from before him with contempt.

10.6.1.en: Do not negotiate with the devil over any sin, for he is evil and may begin by making you fall into laxity over a small sin or negligence in one of the spiritual practices, planning a greater evil for you with time. Persevere in your striving and increase your clinging to God, and the devil will be crushed under your feet.

10.7.s.en: (3) The plague of locusts (the eighth plague)

10.7.0.en: The Lord commanded Moses to stretch out his rod and command the plague of locusts to eat every green plant remaining in Egypt, after the plague of hail had destroyed most of the plants.

10.8.0.en: An east wind carried enormous swarms of locusts over all the land of Egypt, and they ate everything green in it, and because of the multitude of locusts flying in the air, they hid the light of the sun so that it was like dark night.

10.8.1.en: Distance from God robs man of his strength and his material comfort, that perhaps he may return and repent and so find the salvation of his soul.

10.9.s.en: (4) The removal of the plague of locusts

10.9.0.en: Pharaoh felt his helplessness and the ruin of Egypt and its exposure to hunger and certain death, so he summoned Moses and Aaron and declared his fault before them and begged them to remove the locusts from him, and promised to let the people go, and that this would be the last plague they would remove from him.

10.9.1.en: Do not trust the promises of the devil or of the wicked who are his helpers, for he is a deceiver; hold fast to God alone and His commandments.

10.10.0.en: Moses prayed to God, and He sent a west wind, the opposite of the east wind that had carried the locusts to Egypt, and it was stronger than the east wind, so it carried all the locusts out of Egypt and cast them into the Red Sea (the Sea of Reeds), and Egypt was rid of the locusts.

10.10.1.en: God is able to do all things, so do not fear harsh circumstances, however difficult they seem, for God has many ways to resolve them.

10.11.0.en: Pharaoh returned to the hardness of his heart and refused to let the people go.

10.12.s.en: (5) The plague of darkness (the ninth plague)

10.12.0.en: God commanded Moses to stretch out his hand and command the ninth plague, which is the plague of darkness over all the land of Egypt. It is noticeable here that Moses did not threaten Pharaoh before this plague of darkness because of the hardness of his heart and his unreadiness to hear the voice of God. The sun was hidden and there was complete darkness over all the land of Egypt, a thick darkness with no light of moon or stars, and its intensity is expressed by saying that it could almost be felt, as if the darkness were a wall that a person could touch. This plague showed the helplessness of their great god Ra, that is, the sun, which they worshipped. Of course there was great fear in all the land of Egypt, which the Book of Wisdom describes in detail, speaking of the movement of insects and animals in the darkness and the terror that left the Egyptians almost dead.

10.13.0.en: The darkness lasted three days, during which no Egyptian moved from his place because of his fear, and none saw another; but on the other side there was light in the land of Goshen, and this plague did not come upon them as the other plagues did not.

10.13.1.en: This plague signifies the spiritual blindness that afflicts those far from God, while His children enjoy His shining upon them and their ability to discern.

10.13.2.en: If God has revealed Himself to you, hold fast to His commandments and seize the opportunity of your nearness to Him, so that you may enjoy more of His light and be delivered from the darkness of sin.

10.14.s.en: (6) The removal of the plague of darkness

10.14.0.en: Pharaoh returned to negotiate with Moses to let all the people go, men, women and children, but on condition that they not take their flocks with them, for he did not want complete obedience to God because of the hardness of his heart.

10.14.1.en: Do not obey some of the commandments and leave out one commandment, or God's wrath will come upon you. And do not let the devil reign over any of your senses or any of your abilities, however small, and do not be lenient about seeing or possessing anything that can make you fall into sin, because the devil will not rest and will fight you with it to make you fall; so cut off from yourself everything that defiles you, and hold fast to your purity and all God's commandments.

10.15.0.en: Hoof: the singular of hooves, which is the front of the animal's foot, resembling a nail.

10.15.1.en: "Wherewith we must serve the Lord": that is, we cannot worship the Lord without offering sacrifices from the cattle, and we do not know the number of animals we shall sacrifice, so we must take all our cattle.

10.15.2.en: Moses refused, and also asked that they take their cattle with them so that they might be able to offer sacrifices to God.

10.16.0.en: Pharaoh became angry and hardened his heart and refused to obey the word of God; indeed, in his anger he told Moses and Aaron that he did not want to see them again and that they should disappear from before him forever, that is, he refused to meet them forever.

10.16.1.en: Persisting in sin makes man shut before himself the opportunities of repentance until the end, and so he loses the salvation of his soul.

10.17.0.en: Moses agreed to Pharaoh's word that he would not see him again. In Pharaoh's mind was anger against Moses, while in Moses' mind was that Pharaoh would die. This indeed happened when he was drowned in the Red Sea.

10.17.1.en: The announcement of the plague of the firstborn

11.0.s.en: (1) The tenth plague and the spoiling of the Egyptians

11.0.0.en: After the plague of darkness, God spoke to Moses and reassured him that the coming plague would be the last and would be so severe that Pharaoh would send them out of Egypt quickly and drive them out in his great fear of their God. The Lord said this to Moses to strengthen him, so that he would not be disturbed by Pharaoh's coming threats, or those mentioned at the end of the previous chapter, that he would kill him if he saw him again.

11.1.0.en: The Egyptians had humiliated the children of Israel and robbed them of their wages by forcing them into building works, so God wanted to return to them something of their material rights from the Egyptians, and He commanded them to borrow from their Egyptian friends jewels of gold and silver. This is not theft, because it was God who commanded it, and it is the carrying out of His commandments, in order to discipline the Egyptians for their greed, covetousness and exploitation of His people.

11.1.1.en: Do not be unjust and harsh toward others, because the just God sees you and will requite you at the proper time; indeed, He may strengthen the weak person you wronged against you.

11.2.0.en: God gave His people favor in the eyes of the Egyptians, so that on the one hand they loved them, and on the other hand they feared them and their God. So when they asked them for gold, they gave it to them immediately, although they knew that they were departing from Egypt; that is, they tried to appease them in every way, so they gave them whatever they wanted of gold and silver. As for Moses, Pharaoh's servants and the great men of the state feared him.

11.2.1.en: Some doubt that the writer of the book is the prophet Moses, since it says here "the man Moses" and does not say "I"; but the truth is that he speaks with humility, saying "the man," and then declares the greatness of God's work with him.

11.3.s.en: (2) The threat of the plague of the firstborn

11.3.0.en: When Pharaoh called Moses and discussed with him leaving Egypt but without the cattle, Moses rejected this proposal and spoke to him with strength and firmness, and declared to him, as the Lord had commanded him, the tenth plague, the plague of the firstborn, in which God goes out in the form of an angel at midnight and kills every firstborn in all the houses of the Egyptians, whether the firstborn of the king or the firstborn of the manservant and the maidservant, and also the firstborn of the beasts.

11.3.1.en: The firstborn of the Egyptians signifies the firstborn of evil, that is, the greatest and most dreadful evil in you, and midnight signifies the darkness in which sin spreads. Cut off the head of sin and its source so that you may rest from it, for there is no truce with the devil.

11.4.0.en: This plague would be terrifying and beyond the Egyptians' endurance, and would be universal in all the houses, so there would be a great cry in all the houses of the Egyptians.

11.4.1.en: If God allows you a tribulation, do not be content with crying out from its pain, but return to God with repentance, and He will forgive you and heal you of its pains.

11.5.0.en: "Shall not a dog move his tongue": no one will harm them.

11.5.1.en: Moses also declared that God would distinguish His people, so that no harm would touch them or their beasts, but they would be in peace, despite the great suffering of the Egyptians.

11.6.0.en: "Great anger": intense anger, which is a holy anger here because it declares the power of God.

11.6.1.en: Moses also declared to Pharaoh that his servants would come to him and beg him and bow down before him, that perhaps he would be willing to go out from Egypt, he and the children of Israel. That is, Pharaoh would agree and submit and seek Moses' favor out of the great fear in him. The bowing down of his servants means their fear of Moses and not worship of him.

11.6.2.en: After Moses threatened Pharaoh with firm and strong words, Pharaoh became angry and said to him, as was mentioned at the end of (ch. 10), do not appear before me again or I will kill you, and Moses agreed and told him that indeed he would not see him again, because he knew that he would die. Then he went out from Pharaoh in anger and strength.

11.7.0.en: God warned Moses of Pharaoh's stubbornness and informed him that he would refuse his word, and He permits this so that He may be glorified and His power may be shown above all the gods of the Egyptians.

11.7.1.en: Do not be disturbed by the arrogance of the wicked and their power, for God is longsuffering toward them and then disciplines them, and know that they resist the good in you because they are wicked... so stand firm in your faith that you may receive the eternal reward.

11.8.0.en: This is a summary of Pharaoh's reactions to all the plagues, which is that he was still stubborn and did not want to submit to God.

11.8.1.en: The Passover and the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt after the plague of the firstborn

12.0.0.en: The beginning of months: the month of Abib was the seventh in the civil year, and after the Babylonian captivity they also called it Nisan, and God made it the first of the months of the religious year because the slaughter of the Passover lamb takes place at its beginning and the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt took place in it. Thus the Jews came to have a civil year in which the month of Abib is the seventh, and a religious year in which the month of Abib is the first, that is, the difference between the two years is six months. The word Abib means the green ear of grain, because this month comes in the spring; the Copts took the same name and put it in their months, but at another time, which is the summer.

12.0.1.en: After Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh's palace for the last time, God declared to them the most important law in the Old Testament, which is the feast of the Passover, because it is the pivot of the Old Testament, since it clearly signifies the redemption of Christ. So He appointed for them that the month in which they were, the month of Abib, would be the beginning of months and the first of them, meaning that redemption is the foundation of the faith and the beginning of everything, whose results we receive in the New Testament through the Holy Sacraments.

12.1.0.en: "According to the house of their fathers": that is, according to the number of families or households in each tribe.

12.1.1.en: "According to the number of the souls": the number of the members of the household.

12.1.2.en: "Every man according to his eating": that is, the amount of food for adults is more than for children.

12.1.3.en: The law is summed up in that every house takes a lamb to slaughter for itself and eat of it, and the size of the lamb is according to the number of members of the household, that is, Christ satisfies the whole household, large or small. If the household is small, it takes its neighbor with it and the two slaughter one lamb. This neighbor signifies the Gentiles, that is, the people of God proclaim Christ so that the whole world may believe.

12.1.4.en: The time for taking the lamb is the tenth day, and this signifies that after the Ten Commandments in the Old Testament comes Christ the Redeemer.

12.2.0.en: God requires of the lamb that is to be slaughtered the following:

12.2.1.en: "Without blemish": because Christ is a lamb without blemish, that is, without sin.

12.2.2.en: "A male": because Christ is male, that is, a bridegroom to the soul.

12.2.3.en: "Of the first year": that is, full of vitality and youth, as Christ is the source of life.

12.2.4.en: "From the sheep, or from the goats": the sheep or the goat is distinguished by obedience and gentleness, so it signifies Christ, who was obedient unto death and was in constant peace.

12.2.5.en: From this it appears that the Passover lamb is a clear type of the crucified Christ. And the choosing of the lamb as a male is not only because it signifies Christ but also:

12.2.6.en: 1- Because it redeems the males of the children of Israel, who were dying from the severity of the labor or were being killed by Pharaoh by being cast into the river (ch. 1).

12.2.7.en: 2- Because it redeems the male firstborn of the children of Israel at the time when the angel kills the firstborn of Egypt.

12.3.0.en: It is kept until the fourteenth day to make sure of its soundness so that God is not offered anything defective, and the fourteenth day is when the moon is full. The moon signifies the Church, for Christ is the Redeemer of the Church in the perfection of her splendor and brightness. And its remaining four days has other spiritual and psychological meanings, in addition to making sure of its soundness, and these meanings are:

12.3.1.en: 1- The family's feeling that the lamb has become like one of its members, just as Christ lived among the Jews as one of them and then redeemed them and redeemed humanity.

12.3.2.en: 2- Its remaining four days signifies their bondage of 400 years in Egypt.

12.3.3.en: 3- That they might contemplate and think about their salvation, which would be accomplished by the slaughter of the lamb, which signifies Christ.

12.3.4.en: "In the evening": this is what the Jews call the first evening, that is, sunset, when the sun inclines toward the west at the ninth hour, which is three o'clock in the afternoon by present reckoning. The second evening is the disappearance of the sun with all its traces, that is, the red twilight, and this is at the eleventh hour, which is five o'clock in the evening by present reckoning. So the lamb is slaughtered between the two evenings, that is, from the ninth hour to the eleventh, and the Lord Christ died on the Cross at the ninth hour, that is, after the first evening, at the same time as the slaughter of the Passover lamb.

12.4.0.en: After the slaughter of the lamb they take of its blood and strike it on:

12.4.1.en: The two side posts: that is, the sides of the door, right and left, which signifies the Old and New Testaments and also signifies the Jews and the Gentiles, for Christ is the Savior of all.

12.4.2.en: The upper door post: that is, the top of the door, which signifies man's thought and head, that is, the most important part of him; and he did not strike the lower threshold, lest people tread on it when entering the house.

12.5.0.en: "Roast": a symbol of the sufferings of Christ, and they usually roasted it on two skewers crossing each other, that is, in the form of a cross, as a symbol of the crucifixion of Christ.

12.5.1.en: Roasting is also the quickest way to cook meat, so it reminds them of their haste when leaving Egypt.

12.5.2.en: "Unleavened bread": that is, without leaven, because leaven signifies evil and unleavened bread signifies purity, that is, they eat it with a pure heart; and because they were in haste to leave Egypt, their dough did not ferment, so they ate it unleavened after eating the Passover. "Bitter herbs": they signify the bitterness of sin, which is removed by the blood of Christ the Redeemer, that is, the slaughtered, roasted lamb; the bitterness signifies repentance for the sins that embittered the soul, in addition to indicating the bitterness of the bondage they suffered in Egypt.

12.6.0.en: "Raw, nor sodden": this signifies spiritual softness, sloth and laxity, in addition to the fact that raw meat comes with its blood, which the law later forbade, and which was a custom before the law, so that they would not share with the pagans who eat meat with its blood.

12.6.1.en: "His head with his legs, and with the purtenance thereof": that is, we take the whole of Christ within us and do not neglect any of His commandments, even if it seems small like the feet, that is, the legs. And we take the depths of the commandment, that is, the inward parts of the lamb.

12.7.0.en: Because of its holiness and importance it is eaten entire and nothing of it is left, so that it is not exposed to corruption or mixing with any foods. And its burning is to confirm the death of Christ for us and to keep the meat from corruption. Therefore in the New Testament the Church leaves nothing of Christ's sacrifice on the altar after the Liturgy, that is, His Body and Blood. And its being eaten in one night with none of it left until morning reminds them of their eating the Passover and their leaving Egypt in one night and their deliverance from bondage.

12.8.0.en: It is also required in the manner of eating it that they eat it ready to depart, because they would leave Egypt after a few hours, since the angel would strike the firstborn and the Egyptians would ask them to hurry out of Egypt. Readiness to depart is expressed by the following:

12.8.1.en: "With your loins girded": that is, they tie their waists with a leather belt as a sign of readiness for travel or work and striving. These are the characteristics of the one who strives spiritually, that is, no self-indulgence and readiness to labor with energy in worship and service.

12.8.2.en: "Your shoes on your feet": shoes signify protection from the thorns of the ground, which signify the thorns of sin. St. Paul the Apostle tells us that shoes are the preparation of the gospel of peace, that is, carrying out the commandments. "Your staff": the staff signifies the power of God and the Cross and the rod of Moses, that is, that they rely on the power of God. "In haste": quickly, because this shows their attention to it, and because Pharaoh would hurry them to leave Egypt out of his fear after the plague of the firstborn (v. 31). It signifies spiritual wakefulness and attention to spiritual striving, and not putting off Communion because of the busyness of life. "Passover": its meaning is passing over, and in Coptic it is Pascha, a memorial of the destroying angel passing over their houses and killing the firstborn of Egypt; it is the cause of their salvation, for by the blood of the Passover lamb they received salvation.

12.9.0.en: "I will pass through the land of Egypt": the power of God, represented by the destroying angel, passes through all Egypt. The tenth plague, with the other plagues, shows the power of God above all the power of the pagan gods, and it subdues Pharaoh, who was a god, because the firstborn of all, among them Pharaoh's firstborn, will die.

12.10.0.en: It clearly confirms that the protection of the firstborn of His people is by the blood struck on the doors, and it signifies the blood of Christ, which protects us from the devil's wars and which we receive through the Holy Sacraments. So when the angel passes over he sees the blood and does not kill anyone in that house, because of their faith and their obedience to God in slaughtering the lamb and striking the door with the blood.

12.11.0.en: God asked Moses that they not make this Passover once only, but that the feast of the Passover be kept every year, so that they might prepare for the Christ who was coming to redeem them, whom the Passover lamb signifies, and that they continue to keep the Passover throughout their generations until Christ our new Passover comes and redeems us on the Cross.

12.11.1.en: Take care to prepare for partaking of the Holy Sacraments so that they may work in you with power, however difficult the circumstances around you.

12.12.0.en: Leaven signifies evil, so God asked the children of Israel, after keeping the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day, to eat unleavened bread as a sign of purity, and to go on eating it for seven days from the fifteenth day (from the evening of the fourteenth day) until the twenty-first day.

12.12.1.en: "That soul shall be cut off from Israel": set apart and removed from the congregation of the children of Israel.

12.13.0.en: "An holy convocation": that is, this day is set apart for the worship of God and works of goodness.

12.13.1.en: God also adds the keeping of two feasts of unleavened bread, on the first day, which is the fifteenth, and on the last day, which is the twenty-first, in this feast. They come to the tabernacle of the congregation and offer prayers, and a sermon may be added. They eat unleavened bread to show the purity of their hearts, and they free themselves for the feast every year and leave their daily work, doing no material work except the preparing of food.

12.13.2.en: The feasts of the Jews are seven, as mentioned in (Lev 23).

12.13.3.en: Take care to purify the heart by repentance, especially at feasts and spiritual occasions, so that you may be free for the worship of God and the enjoyment of fellowship with Him.

12.14.0.en: "In this selfsame day": that is, the fifteenth day of Nisan.

12.14.1.en: "I brought your armies out": He called them His armies because they are His people, obedient to His commands like soldiers. And He said "I brought out" although they had not yet gone out, because He, exalted is He, had decreed it, so it is certain that He will accomplish it.

12.14.2.en: God required them to continue this law throughout their lives and the lives of their children, for these feasts help toward pure conduct before God, which results from the slaughter of the lamb that signifies the redemption of Christ, for from Him we receive purity in our conduct.

12.15.0.en: "In the first month": that is, the month of Abib, and if a person was defiled for any reason, he keeps it in the following month on the fourteenth day (Num 6:6-13). He declared the importance of holding to the eating of unleavened bread, and whoever violates this is put to death, whether he is:

12.15.1.en: "A stranger": that is, the Jewish proselytes, who are those who joined the Jews and were circumcised, whether from the Egyptians or the Canaanites or any other people.

12.15.2.en: "Born in the land": he means the descendants of Jacob and their children, that is, the original Jews who are not proselytes, whose fathers were born in the land of Canaan, that is, the Promised Land.

12.15.3.en: The first Passover was kept in Egypt and the second in the wilderness of Sinai by Moses, and the third in Canaan by Joshua (Josh 5) after the forty years of wandering in the wilderness, and it was meant to be kept every year as God commanded.

12.15.4.en: Whoever disobeys and rejects God's commandment deserves death, but His mercy is longsuffering toward you, that perhaps you may repent, and it receives you and removes from you the sentence of death by the blood of Christ.

12.16.s.en: (3) Moses teaches the people the law of the Passover

12.16.0.en: Moses commanded all the people that each one should prepare a lamb to slaughter and offer as a Passover to the Lord.

12.17.0.en: Hyssop: a plant like thyme, with stems bearing weak green leaves resembling the parsley plant. If the blood of the Passover lamb signifies the blood of Christ, that is, the work of grace, then the hyssop signifies human striving, which, despite its weakness like the leaves of hyssop, is necessary for receiving salvation.

12.17.1.en: Moses asked them, after the slaughter of the lamb, to pour its blood into a vessel of metal or earthenware called the basin (a small bowl or basin), then to bring a bunch or bundle of the hyssop plant and dip this bundle in the blood and strike with it the upper door post and its two side posts, right and left. He asked them on this night to take shelter inside their houses behind this door marked with blood, and so the destroying angel who would kill the firstborn of the Egyptians would not harm them.

12.17.2.en: Repentance, holding to God's commandments and partaking of His Holy Sacraments protect from God's judgment, and Satan cannot harm you.

12.18.0.en: God passes through, by means of the destroying angel, and sees the blood that protects those inside the house and does not harm them, while the one who does not believe in God and has not struck his door with the blood is exposed to the killing of his firstborn.

12.18.1.en: If you believe, you live reassured, sheltered by God, and fears and anxiety are removed from you, and you live happy as well.

12.19.0.en: He asked them to keep the Passover every year throughout their lives and after their entering the Promised Land.

12.20.0.en: He asked them to teach their children the feast of the Passover, which is a memorial of God's protection of His children from evil, as happened in Egypt in that their firstborn were not killed. The people agreed and declared their submission by bowing down to God, and they went and did what Moses had said, and slaughtered the sheep and struck the doors with the blood.

12.21.s.en: (4) The plague of the firstborn (the tenth plague)

12.21.0.en: After the children of Israel slaughtered the sheep and struck the doors with the blood, the destroying angel passed over their houses at midnight, but he entered all the houses of the Egyptians and killed their firstborn, whether the firstborn of the greatest man, who is Pharaoh, or the weakest man, who is the captive. It seems that the angel's entering was with a loud voice inside the house, which woke everyone, and he killed the firstborn, and the firstborn cried out, and all the members of his house, so there was a cry in all Egypt. And the firstborn, as he was dying, declared the reason for his death, which was the preventing of the children of Israel from going out, as stated in the deuterocanonical books (the Book of Wisdom 18:18).

12.22.0.en: Pharaoh hastened to summon Moses and Aaron during the night and begged them to go out with all the people of Israel and with their flocks to worship God as they wished; indeed, in his great terror he also asked them to bless him, that is, to pray for him, because he feared that their God would kill him.

12.23.0.en: A general feeling prevailed in Egypt that they were all exposed to death, so they urged the children of Israel to go out quickly, fearing them lest they die like their firstborn.

12.23.1.en: God is able to give you grace and awe in the eyes of others, even those who are hostile to you and wrong you, so that they submit to you and fear to wrong you. So do not be disturbed if their wrongs are prolonged, for your God sees everything and stops them at the proper time and turns all their evil to your benefit, and counts for you in heaven every endurance you have endured for His sake.

12.24.1.en: Because of the Egyptians' urging the children of Israel to go out, they hurried to gather their belongings. Their dough was without leaven, so they carried their kneadingtroughs with the dough in them, and the rest they put in their clothes, that is, in sheets or robes, and tied them in bundles and carried them on their shoulders to leave Egypt quickly.

12.24.2.en: "Before it was leavened" does not mean that they were going to put leaven in it, because God commanded them to eat unleavened bread, that is, bread without leaven, but to declare that the flour had been mixed with water only a few hours earlier and therefore could not have become leavened, and they were going to prepare it as cakes of unleavened bread after a few hours, that is, at the dawn of the new day.

12.25.0.en: The children of Israel carried out God's word, so they asked the Egyptians for gold and silver and also clothing, to borrow from them for their journey into the wilderness.

12.26.0.en: God gave the children of Israel awe and fear in the eyes of the Egyptians, so they gave them everything they asked, although they knew that they were going out into the desert and would not return and that what they had borrowed would not be given back to them, and they did this out of terror of the children of Israel. In this the children of Israel recovered something of their rights, for their partial spoiling of the Egyptians was a recovering of something of what the Egyptians had taken from them by forcing them into labor for many years.

12.26.1.en: Do not be disturbed if your rights have been lost for many years, for your God who cares for you will compensate you at the proper time and will give you what is better than them, namely spiritual gifts, so that you receive peace, consolation and rest, in addition to material blessings such as your protection from many dangers into which others may fall, and He gives you the opportunity to be joined to Him and to enjoy fellowship with Him.

12.27.s.en: (6) The departure of the children of Israel from Egypt

12.27.0.en: The children of Israel journeyed from Rameses, which is the province or district at one edge of which lies the city of Tanis, and they moved toward the southeast to the city of Succoth, whose meaning is tents (map 2), because many tents were pitched there, and Succoth is 15 km from Rameses. Rameses lies in the place of the present-day Sharqia governorate, and their direction was southeast, that is, toward present-day Ismailia and south of it. Rameses signifies the corruption from which the spiritual man must depart and go to Succoth, which is the tents, that is, become a stranger to the world and so find God.

12.27.1.en: The number of those who went out was 600 thousand men, and the women were slightly more than that, that is, about 800 thousand, in addition to the children under 18 years, who were about 500 thousand, and to them is added the mixed multitude, who were the slaves and non-Jews who believed in God and were circumcised and joined the Jews, about 100 thousand, so the total is approximately 2 million.

12.27.2.en: And with them was a large number of cattle, which God had blessed so that they became numerous, that they might offer sacrifices to Him as He wished.

12.27.3.en: The number (6) signifies the perfection of human work, because God completed the creation of the world in six days and on the sixth day created man, while the number (100) signifies the community and the number (1000) signifies eternity, so the symbolic meaning of 600 thousand is the perfection of the human work of the community believing in God, departing from Egypt, whose goal is life with God in the wilderness in order to obtain heavenly life.

12.27.4.en: You need to leave the places of sin and become a stranger to the world in order to see God. So give up your pleasure and comfort to find God, for many material things can occupy you and turn your inclinations and ambitions toward them; so set limits for them and use them in measure, that you may continue and grow in your love for God.

12.28.0.en: "Cakes" of bread: dough baked on stones heated by the rays of the sun, which they leave until it is done.

12.28.1.en: When they reached Succoth they pitched their tents and baked their dough on stones scattered in the desert, and the dough was unleavened, without leaven, because they had gone out of Egypt quickly.

12.29.s.en: (7) The time of the departure of the children of Israel

12.29.0.en: 1- This verse makes clear, in a definite way, that the length of the time the people of the children of Israel were in the land of Egypt was 430 years, especially since the prophet Moses expressed this matter precisely in his saying, "the sojourning of the children of Israel, who dwelt in Egypt" (v. 40) and then "at the end of the four hundred and thirty years" (v. 41). It is also noticed that the prophet Moses is an eyewitness of this period and lived the last part of it himself in Egypt with his people.

12.29.1.en: 2- This period is also mentioned in two other places in the Bible as 400 years, and this is an approximation, but precisely it is 430 years as we have mentioned, and these two places are:

12.29.2.en: a- When God spoke to Abram in (Gen 15:13) and told him that his seed would be a stranger in a land that is not theirs for 400 years.

12.29.3.en: b- When Stephen spoke before his martyrdom (Acts 7:6) and said that the seed of Abraham would sojourn for 400 years in a strange land, where they would be enslaved.

12.29.4.en: 3- St. Paul the Apostle mentions in (Gal 3:16, 17) that this period is 430 years, and because he says that it is from Abraham until Moses, who received the Law, some thought that it begins from Abraham until Moses, and therefore the period they spent in Egypt would be less than 430 years. But if we look closely at (Gal 3:16) we notice that he says "to Abraham and his seed," and by his seed is meant Jacob, who entered Egypt with his twelve sons and his grandchildren, and they spent 430 years there. At the same time, by the seed of Abraham is meant Christ, in whom is fulfilled the accomplishment of the promises of salvation in the fullness of time.

12.30.0.en: On the night in which the angel killed the firstborn of Egypt, that is, the fifteenth day of the month of Abib, all the children of Israel went out, and He calls them "the hosts of the Lord" because they believe in Him and are submissive to Him in a serious life like soldiers.

12.30.1.en: You are a soldier of Christ against Satan, so hold fast to your spiritual weapons, and God is able to bring you out of all his schemes and snares.

12.31.0.en: The night of the departure of the children of Israel from Egypt is considered a great night, because in it the power of God was shown, which protects His children and delivers them from evil, so they should remember it and keep a feast for it and thank God for it.

12.32.0.en: It declares that the Passover belongs only to the circumcised Jews and that no stranger, sojourner or guest among them may eat of it, as happens now in the Church of the New Testament, for no one can partake of the Holy Sacraments except one who has received Baptism, which circumcision signifies. And the foreign slave whom the Jew buys and who lives in his house, he circumcises first so that he may join the faith, and then he eats of the Passover. This slave bought with silver signifies the believing person owned by Christ.

12.33.0.en: It makes clear that the household eats the Passover inside the house, as the faithful eat the Body and Blood of the Lord inside the Church, and do not take it out except in the case of the sick person unable to come to church.

12.33.1.en: It also requires that no bone of the Passover lamb be broken, as happened with Christ, for His bones were not broken but He died slaughtered, by internal bleeding.

12.33.2.en: The bones are the strong part inside the body, so they signify the truth and the faith that is not broken; then it is said of the saints that God keeps their bones, not one of them is broken, that is, their faith is firm and does not change (Ps 34:20). All the members of the household would gather inside the house, sheltered behind the blood struck on the door, and this means the oneness of the household and its taking shelter under the blood of Christ. They slaughtered the Passover the first time in their houses, then they slaughtered it before the tabernacle of the congregation after it was set up. And when the Temple was established in Canaan they would come to Jerusalem and slaughter it before the house of the Lord, because the Passover is one of the three great feasts at which all the males of the children of Israel had to appear at the house of the Lord, namely the feasts of the Passover, of Pentecost and of Tabernacles (Deut 16:5, 6, 16).

12.34.0.en: It decrees here that all the children of Israel keep the Passover, for it is the condition of their membership in the people of God, just as Communion is the condition of a Christian's membership in the Church.

12.35.0.en: Here He confirmed the necessity of circumcision as a condition for whoever eats the Passover, and this for the second time in the same passage because of the importance of the matter. And all the children of Israel obeyed this law, so God kept their firstborn and brought them out of Egypt on this night with great power.

12.35.1.en: Enjoy the greatest grace in existence, which is partaking of the Holy Sacraments, for it is the greatest power you receive and the one in which you are unique among all mankind, and it protects you and saves you from the devil's wars and carries you across to eternity. A comparison between the Passover lamb and the sacrifice of Christ, which is signified by the series The Passover lamb The sacrifice of Christ

12.35.3.en: 2- A lamb without blemish (v. 5) Christ is a lamb without blemish

12.35.4.en: 3- Of the first year (v. 5) signifies the innocence, purity and vitality of Christ

12.35.5.en: 4- It is kept from the tenth day until the fourteenth Christ remained in Jerusalem four days before in their houses (vv. 3-6) His crucifixion, from Monday of the Pascha (corresponding to the tenth of Nisan) until He was crucified on Friday, which is the fourteenth of Nisan.(

12.35.6.en: 5- It is slaughtered between the two evenings, that is, between the third Christ gave up His spirit on the Cross at and the fifth in the evening, which is the ninth hour the ninth hour.

12.35.8.en: 6- The doors are struck with blood, so that it protects those inside by the blood of Christ we are saved from death, that is, we do not the house (v. 7) perish but live in it.

12.35.9.en: 7- The lamb is one of the clean animals (v. 5) Christ is pure and holy

12.35.10.en: 8- The lamb was roasted with fire (vv. 8, 9) Christ passed through the sufferings alone and bore the fire of the divine wrath and redeemed us

12.35.11.en: 9- The whole lamb is roasted, its head and its legs with Christ bore all the spiritual, psychological and its inwards (v. 9) and bodily sufferings.

12.35.12.en: 10- Not a bone of it is broken (v. 46) The bones of Christ were not broken on the Cross

12.35.13.en: 11- Unleavened bread was eaten with it (v. 8) Christ is pure and clean.

12.35.14.en: 12- It is eaten with bitter herbs (v. 9) Christ bore the bitter sufferings on the Cross

12.35.15.en: 13- They ate it standing, with their loins girded, The believers who eat the Body of Christ and with their staves in their hands and their shoes on their feet and His Blood are always ready to depart in readiness for their departure from Egypt (v. 11). from the world and enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.

12.35.16.en: 14 They ate it on the same night and left none of it Christ accomplished our redemption on the Cross in one until the morning (v. 10) day, and we eat His Body and Blood on the same day and leave none of it for the next day

12.35.17.en: 15- God commanded them to keep the Passover as an everlasting ordinance Christ commanded His Church to offer the sacrifice of His Body the series The Passover lamb The sacrifice of Christ throughout their generations (vv. 14, 24, 25) and Blood throughout their life on earth.

12.35.18.en: 16- Only the circumcised among the Jews ate it Only the believers in Christ who have received holy Baptism and the proselytes (vv. 43, 44, 48, 49) eat the Body and Blood of the Lord.

12.35.19.en: 17- Both great and small ate of it, that is, all members of Both great and small eat the Body and Blood of Christ, that is, all the household (v. 4) the believers

12.35.20.en: 18- All the Jews had to keep the Passover (v. 47) All the believers of the Church must partake of the Body and and share in eating it Blood of the Lord, that is, be in one fellowship.

12.35.21.en: 19- No one who was defiled for any reason ate of it Only the penitent and those who have received the Sacrament of Confession (Num 6:6-9). partake of the Body and Blood of Christ. The consecration of the firstborn, the wandering of the people and God's leading.
